Measuring heat change by recording temperature rise

walkthroughs.body_html:
Same idea, opposite signs.

Hand warmers use an exothermic reaction — e.g. iron oxidising, or sodium acetate crystallising. Heat flows out into your fingers.

Cold packs use an endothermic reaction — e.g. ammonium nitrate dissolving in water. Heat flows in from the injury, cooling it.

Reusable warmers can be 'reset' by boiling — the reaction is reversible.

To compare fuels, burn a known mass under a metal can of water. Measure the temperature rise.

Energy released = mass of water × 4.2 × temperature rise (in joules).

Then energy per gram = energy released ÷ mass of fuel burned.

Higher J/g means a better fuel. Heat losses to the air make experimental values lower than the true values.

Hess's law says: the total energy change depends only on the start and end, not the route taken.

So if you go from reactants to products directly, or via a longer path, ΔH adds up to the same number.

This is useful when ΔH can't be measured directly — you go around the back via reactions you can measure.

mcqs.q: A sports cold pack contains ammonium nitrate and water. When squeezed, it gets cold. The reaction is.
options: Exothermic — releases heat
Endothermic — takes in heat
Neither
Combustion

mcqs.q: Why is the experimental value for a fuel's energy per gram usually lower than the true value?
options: The thermometer reads too high
Heat is lost to the surroundings
The fuel weighs more than expected
Water absorbs no heat

mcqs.q: In an exothermic reaction, what happens energetically with the bonds?
options: Bond breaking releases energy and bond making absorbs energy.
Energy released forming new bonds exceeds energy absorbed breaking existing bonds.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
The reactants get colder because they lose mass as energy.

mcqs.q: Where is almost all the mass of an atom located?
options: Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Electrons contribute significantly to the mass of an atom.
Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
In the nucleus, made up of protons and neutrons.

mcqs.q: What is different between two isotopes of the same element?
options: Isotopes are atoms of different elements with the same mass.
They have the same number of protons but different numbers of neutrons.
Mass is spread evenly throughout the entire atom including the electron shells.
Isotopes have different numbers of electrons, which is why their mass differs.
